claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi's component state migrations are a new feature.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.

The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, creating a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and association, and an internet gateway, with a security group outside the component.
Replacing an AWS VPC forces replacement of a security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation).
Without a migration connecting old state to new code, upgrading from legacy AWSX VPC could replace the VPC instead of keeping it.
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

The Pulumi resource trees for the example: v1 has awsx:x:ec2:Vpc with Subnet and InternetGateway component wrappers; v2 has awsx:ec2:Vpc containing aws Vpc with subnet and internet gateway; v3 has aws Vpc as root.
Pulumi state records both physical resources and components; each record has a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud provider ID.

Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components; modern AWSX removes those wrappers, and in the example the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
Pulumi resource options accept a `stateMigrations` option taking a migration callback, alongside an alias for the legacy component type.

The state migration callback receives the aliased component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (complete replacement records) and `successors` (map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses successor mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, such as the security group's reference to the VPC.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, and a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration.

After a migration changes saved state, Pulumi compares the new program with that state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Running `pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and the update (`pulumi up`) saves the migrated state.
When users upgrade a component that registers a migration, Pulumi runs the migration automatically as part of normal preview and update, without users writing the migration or editing stack state.
A component state migrations guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering the callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repo contains aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration with v1, v2, v3 programs and migration.ts files.
A component state migrations discussion exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
Pulumi state migration callbacks run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
Each successor mapping returned by a component state migration callback connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing results from component state migrations (with update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
